questions.q: Let $P$ be a parabola with vertex  $\left(2, 3\right)$ and directrix $2x + y = 6$. Let an ellipse $E: \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1, a > b$ of eccentricity $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ pass through the focus of the parabola $P$. Then the square of the length of the latus rectum of $E$, is
questions.solution:
Let $Z$ be the foot of perpendicular from vertex to directrix of parabola,

Now, finding $Z$ we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 2}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = - \dfrac{\left(4 + 3\right) - 6}{4 + 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 2}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{- 1}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 2}{2} = \dfrac{- 1}{5}, \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{- 1}{5}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{12}{5}, y = \dfrac{16}{5}$

$⇒ Z ≡ \left(\dfrac{12}{5}, \dfrac{16}{5}\right)$

Eccentricity of ellipse is given as $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Now, finding ${b}^{2}$ using eccentricity formula we get,

$⇒ {b}^{2} = {a}^{2}\left(1 - {e}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{2}$

So, equation of ellipse will be,

$⇒ \dfrac{144}{25{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{256}{25 \times \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{2}} = 1$ {as $\left(x, y\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{12}{5}, \dfrac{16}{5}\right)$ }

$⇒ \dfrac{144}{25{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{512}{25{a}^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{656}{25{a}^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ {a}^{2} = \dfrac{656}{25}$

$⇒ {b}^{2} = \dfrac{328}{25}$

Length of latus rectum is given by,
$L = \dfrac{2{b}^{2}}{a}$.

$⇒ L = \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{328}{25}}{\dfrac{\sqrt{656}}{5}}$

$⇒ L = \dfrac{\sqrt{656}}{5}$

$⇒ {L}^{2} = \dfrac{656}{25}$

questions.q: Let $P$ be a point on the ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{4} = 1$. Let the line passing through $P$ and parallel to $y -$axis meet the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 9$ at point $Q$ such that $P\text{and}Q$ are on the same side of the $x -$axis. Then, the eccentricity of the locus of the point $R$ on $PQ$ such that $PR: RQ = 4: 3$ as $P$ moves on the ellipse, is:
questions.solution:
Given equation of ellipse and circle are $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{4} = 1$ and ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 9$.

$⇒ P ≡ \left(3cos\theta, 2sin\theta\right)\text{and}Q ≡ \left(3cos\theta, 3sin\theta\right)$

Let, $R ≡ \left(h, k\right)$

$⇒ h = 3cos\theta, k = \dfrac{18}{7}sin\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{h}{3} = cos\theta, \dfrac{7k}{18} = sin\theta$

So, locus of $R$ is given by, $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} + \dfrac{49{y}^{2}}{324} = 1$.

$⇒ e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{324}{49 \times 9}}$

$⇒ e = \dfrac{\sqrt{117}}{21}$

$⇒ e = \dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{7}$

questions.q: The maximum area of a triangle whose one vertex is at $( 0, 0 )$ and the other two vertices lie on the curve $y = - 2{x}^{2} + 54$ at points $( x, y )$ and $( - x, y )$ where $y > 0$ is :
questions.solution:
Let, area of triangle $ABC$ be denoted by $P$.

$⇒ P = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}0 & 0 & 1 \\ x & y & 1 \\ - x & y & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ P = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|0 - 0 + 2xy\right|$

$⇒ P = \left|xy\right|$

$⇒ P = \left|x\left(- 2{x}^{2} + 54\right)\right|$

$⇒ P = \left|- 2{x}^{3} + 54x\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{dP}{dx} = \left|- 6{x}^{2} + 54\right|$

For critical points, $\dfrac{dP}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ \left|- 6{x}^{2} + 54\right| = 0$

$⇒ x = \pm 3$

So, the maximum area will be,

$A = 3 ( - 2 \times 9 + 54 )$

$⇒ A = 108$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 3 \mathrm{x}+4 \mathrm{y}=12 \\ & 3(\mathrm{r} \cos \theta)+4(\mathrm{r} \sin \theta)=12 \\ & \mathrm{r}(3 \cos \theta+4 \sin \theta)=12 \ldots(1) \\ & 3(-\mathrm{r} \sin \theta)+4(\mathrm{r} \cos \theta)=12 \\ & \mathrm{r}(-3 \sin \theta+4 \cos \theta)=12 \ldots(2) \\ & \left(\frac{12}{\mathrm{r}}\right)^2+\left(\frac{12}{\mathrm{r}}\right)^2=(3 \cos \theta+4 \sin \theta)^2+(-3 \sin \theta+4 \cos \theta)^2 \\ & 2\left(\frac{12}{\mathrm{r}}\right)^2=9+16 \\ & \frac{2 \times 144}{\mathrm{r}^2}=25 \Rightarrow 288=25 \mathrm{r}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{288}{25}=\mathrm{r}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{2}\left(\frac{12}{5}\right)=\mathrm{r} \\ & \ell=\mathrm{OP}^2+\mathrm{PQ}^2+\mathrm{QO}^2 \\ & \ell=\mathrm{r}^2+\mathrm{r}^2 \quad+\mathrm{r}^2(\cos \theta+\sin \theta)^2+\mathrm{r}^2(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)^2 \\ & =2 \mathrm{r}^2+\mathrm{r}^2(1+\sin 2 \theta+1-2 \sin 2 \theta) \\ & =2 \mathrm{r}^2+2 \mathrm{r}^2 \\ & =4 \mathrm{r}^2 \\ & =4\left(\frac{288}{25}\right)=\frac{1152}{25}=46.08 \\ & {[\ell]=46}\end{aligned}$

If the point $C$ lies on $2x - y = 5$ and the point $D$ lies on $3x - 2y = 6$, then the value of $\left|\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta\right|$ is equal to ______.

And the point $C$ lies on $2x - y = 5$ and the point $D$ lies on $3x - 2y = 6$,

Now, using the midpoint formula we get,

$P ≡ \left(\dfrac{\alpha - 2}{2}, \dfrac{\beta - 1}{2}\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{\gamma + 1}{2}, \dfrac{\delta}{2}\right)$

Now, on comparing we get,

$\dfrac{\alpha - 2}{2} = \dfrac{\gamma + 1}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\beta - 1}{2} = \dfrac{\delta}{2}$

$⇒ \alpha - \gamma = 3 . . . ( 1 ) , \beta - \delta = 1 . . . ( 2 )$

Also, given $\left(\gamma, \delta\right)$ lies on $3x - 2y = 6$

$⇒ 3\gamma - 2\delta = 6 . . . \left(3\right)$

And $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ lies on $2x - y = 5$

$⇒ 2\alpha - \beta = 5 . . . ( 4 )$

$\alpha = - 3, \beta = - 11, \gamma = - 6, \delta = - 12$

Hence, $\left|\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta\right| = \left|- 3 - 11 - 6 - 12\right| = 32$

questions.q: Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle in which $A$ is at $\left(- 1, 0\right), ∠ A = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}, AB = AC$ and $B$ is on the positive $x -$axis. If $BC = 4\sqrt{3}$  and the line $BC$ intersects the line $y = x + 3$ at $\left(\alpha, \beta\right),$ then $\dfrac{{\beta}^{4}}{{\alpha}^{2}}$ is:
questions.solution:
Let, $B ≡ \left(p, 0\right)$

$⇒ AB = p + 1, p > 1$

Now, finding point $C$ using parametric form we get,

$\dfrac{x + 1}{cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}} = \dfrac{y - 0}{sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}} = p + 1$

$⇒ C ≡ \left(\dfrac{- p}{2} - \dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\left(p + 1\right)\right)$

$⇒ B{C}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{- 3}{2}\left(p + 1\right)\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\left(p + 1\right)\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ BC = \sqrt{3}\left(p + 1\right) = 4\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ p = 3$

So, $C ≡ \left(- 3, 2\sqrt{3}\right)$

Now, equation of line $BC$ is given by,

$y = \dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{3}}\left(x - 3\right)$

Solving with line $y = x + 3$.

$⇒ x + 3 = \dfrac{3 - x}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ x\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{3} = 3 - x$

$⇒ x\left(\sqrt{3} + 1\right) = 3\left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right)$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{3\left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right)}{1 + \sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{- 3}{2}\left(4 - 2\sqrt{3}\right)$

$⇒ \alpha = - 3\left(2 - \sqrt{3}\right)\text{and}\beta = - 3 + 3\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\beta}^{4}}{{\alpha}^{2}} = \dfrac{81{\left(\sqrt{3} - 1\right)}^{4}}{9{\left(2 - \sqrt{3}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\beta}^{4}}{{\alpha}^{2}} = \dfrac{9{\left(4 - 2\sqrt{3}\right)}^{2}}{{\left(2 - \sqrt{3}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\beta}^{4}}{{\alpha}^{2}} = 36$
